title: Fennel's Brave Boat Ride
markdown:
Coco the cockapoo’s tail did a happy little thump-thump-thump against the soft sun-warmed grass. It was a happy sound, like a little drumbeat. Her friend Fennel the frog sat on his favourite lily pad by the edge of the big shimmering pond. He looked a little bit wobbly. His big thoughtful eyes were wide, and his little froggy fingers were clasped tightly.

“Oh, Coco,” Fennel whispered, his voice like the softest rustle of leaves. “The blackberries on Sunbeam Island look so plump and purple today. I can see them sparkling from here.” He pointed a slightly trembling webbed hand toward a small sunny island in the middle of the pond. “But the pond looks so very, very big.”

Coco padded closer. The sweet damp smell of dewdrops on clover tickled her nose. Sunbeam Island was famous for its blackberries. People said they tasted like sunshine. They were also very, very juicy, like a summer rain shower. Fennel was a little bit nervous about going on the water. He liked his lily pad. It stayed put, his safe floaty home.

“Don’t worry, Fennel,” Coco said, her voice as warm as a soft happy sigh. She nudged a large bright yellow leaf that had drifted down from the big oak tree. It was shaped like a little boat and floated perfectly on the pond’s surface, which mirrored the sky like a fallen piece of blue. “It’s a sunshine boat. We can sail on it right to the island.”

Fennel looked at the yellow leaf. It did look cheerful, like a piece of captured sunshine. But then he looked at the pond again. It shimmered and spread out. His little froggy knees felt like they might do a jig all on their own. “A boat?” he croaked, a tiny puff of air. A little flutter in his tummy, like a tiny moth.

“Yes. A super-duper leaf boat,” Coco explained, her tail giving another hopeful thump. “It will carry us right to the yummiest, juiciest blackberries ever. If you like, you can hold onto my fur. It’s very soft and warm, like a fluffy cloud.” Fennel imagined the plump purple blackberries, glistening like tiny jewels. He imagined Coco’s warm soft fur.

He took a deep wobbly breath. “Okay, Coco. Let’s try.”

With Coco’s gentle encouragement, Fennel carefully hopped onto the sunshine boat. It dipped slightly, making him feel a little fluttery inside. Then Coco, paws placed very carefully, hopped on beside him. The bright yellow leaf bobbed and dipped, and Fennel’s legs did a tiny tremble, like a leaf in a very small breeze. But Coco’s fur was just as warm and soft as she had promised, and her happy panting breath was a steady rhythm beside him.

“We’re floating,” Fennel whispered, his eyes still a little wide, but also filled with a new feeling: wonder. The pond water rippled gently around them, like a soft blue blanket being tucked around their boat. A little breeze, smelling of damp earth and sweet wild clover, began to tickle their noses. It made the yellow leaf boat dance and sway just a little, like it was doing a gentle waltz on the water. The yellow leaf dipped, papery beneath his tiny webbed feet, and the sight of the water shimmering so far below made his tummy do a flip.

“Whee,” chirped Coco. “The wind is helping us fly.” The sunbeams were warm on Fennel’s back, chasing away lingering wobbly feelings. The breeze was not trying to push them anywhere scary. It just made their journey feel like a happy gentle sway.

Soon, with a soft little nudge, the sunshine boat bumped gently against the sandy shore of Sunbeam Island. The bushes were heavy with the biggest, purplest blackberries Fennel had ever seen. They shimmered in the sunlight, so plump and ready they looked like tiny edible jewels. The air itself smelled deliciously sweet.

Fennel hopped off, his legs still a tiny bit wobbly, but his heart feeling much bigger. He carefully picked a blackberry, its skin smooth and cool. He popped it into his mouth. It was bursting with sweet juicy flavour, a tiny explosion of sunshine, even better than he had imagined. He looked at Coco, already happily munching, her tail a golden blur.

“You did it, Fennel,” Coco said, mouth full of berry goodness. “You were so brave. And these blackberries are the bestest ever.”

Fennel smiled, a real happy froggy smile that spread all the way to his ears. He looked out at the pond. It did not seem quite so big anymore. The sunshine boat bobbled gently in the shallow water, a perfect happy yellow against the clear blue, waiting like a small sun that had learned to float.
